```{python}
# | label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from IPython.display import Markdown

# Locate the repository root, so this report may live at any depth under it.
_root = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]
             if (p / "pixi.toml").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(_root / "src"))
from arkhinfra import v3_common as c  # noqa: E402

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",   # full Cyrillic coverage for figure labels
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
})

ACCENT, RISK, GREEN, PURPLE = c.ACCENT, c.RISK, c.GREEN, c.PURPLE
MIXED, OLD = c.MIXED, c.OLD
INK = "#1f2933"

# Provenance keeps a fixed three-hue assignment, never cycled.  The triple was
# checked for colour-vision separation against the page surface; every chart
# using it also carries a legend or direct labels, so hue is never the only cue.
PROV_COLORS = {
    "Confirmed by 2GIS + OSM": GREEN,
    "2GIS only": PURPLE,
    "OSM only": ACCENT,
}
PROV_ORDER = ["Confirmed by 2GIS + OSM", "2GIS only", "OSM only"]


def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v / total * 100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8, color=INK)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.16)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: load
v3 = c.load_v3()
v1 = c.load_v1()
ref22 = c.load_ref_2022_local()

v3["category_en"] = v3["category_orig"].map(c.CATEGORY_EN).fillna(v3["category_orig"])
v3["provenance"] = v3["verification_status"].map(c.STATUS_EN)

n_obj = len(v3)
n_cat = v3["category_orig"].nunique()
n_type = v3["type_orig"].nunique()
n_okrug = v3["okrug_key"].nunique()

OKRUG_ORDER = v3["okrug_key"].value_counts().index.tolist()
three = v3[v3["okrug_key"].isin(c.OKRUGS_2022)]
```

# Introduction

The third delivery (`data/raw_v3/`, generated 2026-08-31) is **not an increment on
the second**. It replaces the city-wide export outright and drops both artefacts
the second delivery was built around — the 2022↔2026 record comparison workbook
and its per-okrug summary. What arrives instead is a fresh city-wide export, a
commercial directory dump that has no precedent in earlier deliveries, and a
rebuilt indicator panel.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-delivery
# | tbl-cap: "What each delivery shipped. The third delivery replaces rather than extends the second."
rows = [
    ["Main object export", "7,228 obj. (city)", "5,257 obj. (3 okrugs)", f"{n_obj:,} obj. (city)"],
    ["Record comparison vs 2022", "—", "2,293 x 5,257", "— (withdrawn)"],
    ["Per-okrug comparison summary", "—", "yes", "— (withdrawn)"],
    ["Commercial directory dump", "—", "—", "10,557 records"],
    ["ARKTMED indicator panel", "—", "28 ind. / 168 rows", "22 ind. / 65 rows"],
    ["2GIS provider present", "yes", "no", "yes"],
]
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(
    rows, columns=["Artefact", "1st (raw)", "2nd (raw_v2)", "3rd (raw_v3)"]
).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## The headline of this delivery

- The **okrug-assignment defect is fixed city-wide**. The first export put 71 % of
  all objects in Oktyabrsky; here the largest okrug holds 35 %, and Isakogorsky
  and Tsiglomensky — merged into one label in the first export — are separate.
- **2GIS is back.** The second delivery was OSM-only; here 759 objects carry 2GIS
  coverage and 172 are independently corroborated by both providers.
- The export is a **fresh census, not a revision**: 81 % of its content in the
  three 2022 okrugs has no counterpart in the 2022 benchmark.
- The **ARKTMED panel is no longer synthetic** — but it lost every health outcome
  indicator it used to carry.

# Part I — source provenance and verification {#sec-provenance}

```{python}
# | label: fig-provenance
# | fig-cap: "Source provenance of the third-delivery export. Independent corroboration remains the exception."
counts = v3["provenance"].value_counts().reindex(PROV_ORDER)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 2.6))
left = 0
for label in PROV_ORDER:
    val = counts[label]
    ax.barh([0], [val], left=left, color=PROV_COLORS[label],
            label=f"{label} — {val:,} ({val / n_obj * 100:.1f}%)")
    if val / n_obj > 0.05:
        ax.text(left + val / 2, 0, f"{val:,}", ha="center", va="center",
                color="white", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    left += val
ax.set_yticks([])
ax.set_xlabel("Objects")
ax.set_title("Provenance of the 2026 export")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.35), ncol=1, fontsize=8, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Only **172 objects (2.4 %)** are confirmed by both providers. The export is
overwhelmingly a single-source OSM product with a 2GIS minority; a
"`confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm`" label therefore marks a small privileged subset,
not the normal case.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-provenance-okrug
# | tbl-cap: "Provenance by okrug. Confirmation rates are uniformly low; no okrug is systematically better covered."
t = pd.crosstab(v3["okrug_key"], v3["provenance"]).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER)
t = t.reindex(columns=PROV_ORDER, fill_value=0)
t["Total"] = t.sum(axis=1)
t["Confirmed %"] = (100 * t["Confirmed by 2GIS + OSM"] / t["Total"]).map("{:.1f}".format)
t["2GIS reach %"] = (100 * (t["Confirmed by 2GIS + OSM"] + t["2GIS only"]) / t["Total"]).map("{:.1f}".format)
t["Total"] = t["Total"].map("{:,}".format)
Markdown(t.rename(columns={"Confirmed by 2GIS + OSM": "Both", "2GIS only": "2GIS",
                           "OSM only": "OSM"}).to_markdown(disable_numparse=True))
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-provenance-class
# | fig-cap: "2GIS reach by 2022-taxonomy class. Tobacco outlets and sport objects depend most on 2GIS; alcohol shops and industrial objects are OSM-only throughout."
cls = [x for x in c.CLASS_ORDER if (v3["category_2022"] == x).any()]
share = pd.crosstab(v3["category_2022"], v3["provenance"], normalize="index") * 100
share = share.reindex(cls).reindex(columns=PROV_ORDER, fill_value=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
left = np.zeros(len(share))
for label in PROV_ORDER:
    ax.barh(share.index, share[label], left=left, color=PROV_COLORS[label], label=label)
    left += share[label].to_numpy()
ax.set_xlabel("Share of objects, %")
ax.set_title("Provenance mix by 2022-taxonomy class")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.invert_yaxis()
# Below the axes: every bar spans the full width, so any in-plot legend would
# sit on top of data.
ax.legend(loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.16), ncol=3,
          fontsize=7, frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The export's internal cross-source check

The export ships its own 2GIS↔OSM reconciliation in `match_distance_meters` and
`match_name_similarity`, populated for 6,785 objects.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-internal-match
# | tbl-cap: "The export's own cross-source agreement. Where the two providers meet, they agree almost exactly."
d = v3["match_distance_meters"].dropna()
s = v3["match_name_similarity"].dropna()
rows = [
    ["Records carrying a cross-source score", f"{len(d):,}", f"{len(d) / n_obj * 100:.1f}% of export"],
    ["Distance exactly 0 m", f"{(d == 0).sum():,}", f"{(d == 0).mean() * 100:.1f}% of scored"],
    ["Distance above 20 m", f"{(d > 20).sum():,}", f"max {d.max():.1f} m"],
    ["Name similarity = 1.00", f"{(s >= 0.999).sum():,}", f"{(s >= 0.999).mean() * 100:.1f}% of scored"],
    ["Name similarity below 0.50", f"{(s < 0.5).sum():,}", "residual disagreements"],
]
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Measure", "Value", "Note"]).to_markdown(index=False))
```

The distribution is degenerate: 99.5 % of scored records sit at exactly 0 m and
99.8 % at a name similarity of exactly 1.00. This is a **deduplication key, not
an independent verification** — it records that the same string at the same point
was seen twice, which is a much weaker claim than two sources independently
attesting an object.

## Field completeness

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness
# | fig-cap: "Attribute completeness, third delivery against the first. Completeness is unchanged; the export improved its okrugs, not its attributes."
fields = ["adress_orig", "latitude", "opening_hours_orig", "phone_orig",
          "website_orig", "opening_date_orig"]
labels = ["Address", "Coordinates", "Opening hours", "Phone", "Website", "Opening date"]
cur = [v3[f].notna().mean() * 100 for f in fields]
old = [v1[f].notna().mean() * 100 for f in fields]
y = np.arange(len(fields))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.0))
ax.barh(y + 0.20, old, height=0.38, color=OLD, label="1st delivery")
ax.barh(y - 0.20, cur, height=0.38, color=ACCENT, label="3rd delivery")
for i, v in enumerate(cur):
    ax.text(v, i - 0.20, f" {v:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_yticks(y, labels)
ax.set_xlim(0, 118)          # room for the 100% direct label
ax.set_xlabel("Records with the field populated, %")
ax.set_title("Attribute completeness")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
# Upper right is the only quadrant free of bars (opening date sits at 1%).
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

`website_check_status` is **empty for all `{python} f"{n_obj:,}"` records** — the
column exists but was never populated, so no website was validated. `opening_date_orig`
is present for 0.6 % of objects, which rules out any analysis of when objects appeared.

# Part III — recoding into the 2022 taxonomy {#sec-recode}

The 2022 study used a seven-class health taxonomy. `recode_2022()` maps the 2026
export onto it from `category_orig`, `type_orig` and the object name, in that
priority order. The full rule set and the resulting crosswalk are in
`docs/crosswalk_2022.md`.

::: {.callout-note}
## A defect inherited from the earlier reports

The copy of this rule in `analysis/v1/eda.qmd` and `analysis/v2/eda-v2.qmd` lowercases
the type field and then tests it against a **capitalised** list of grocery types.
The test can never succeed, so the `Grocery shops` class is empty in every
previously delivered report and its objects were absorbed into
`Other (outside 2022 scheme)`. The rule is corrected here: it moves
**811 objects (11.2 %)** of this export, 854 of the first export, and 392 of the
1,753 records in the 2022 benchmark — 22 % of the benchmark. Counts of
`Other` in the first- and second-delivery reports are inflated accordingly.
:::

```{python}
# | label: fig-recode
# | fig-cap: "The 2026 export recoded into the 2022 health taxonomy."
counts = v3["category_2022"].value_counts().reindex(
    [x for x in c.CLASS_ORDER if (v3["category_2022"] == x).any()])
barh(counts, "Objects by 2022-taxonomy class", "Objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode-compare
# | tbl-cap: "The 2022 taxonomy across the three sources. The 2022 benchmark was built to the taxonomy; the 2026 export is a general-purpose census in which 63% of objects fall outside it."
cls = [x for x in c.CLASS_ORDER]
t = pd.DataFrame({
    "2022 benchmark": ref22["category_2022"].value_counts().reindex(cls, fill_value=0),
    "1st delivery": v1["category_2022"].value_counts().reindex(cls, fill_value=0),
    "3rd delivery": v3["category_2022"].value_counts().reindex(cls, fill_value=0),
})
t["3rd, % of export"] = (100 * t["3rd delivery"] / n_obj).map("{:.1f}".format)
for col in ["2022 benchmark", "1st delivery", "3rd delivery"]:
    t[col] = t[col].map("{:,}".format)
# tabulate re-parses numeric-looking strings and drops the formatting, so the
# pre-formatted columns need number parsing switched off.
Markdown(t.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True))
```

The 2022 benchmark was assembled *to* this taxonomy, so only 7 of its records fall
outside it. The 2026 export is a general-purpose census: 63 % of it is outside the
2022 scheme. Comparisons between the two must therefore be made class by class,
never on totals.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode-okrug
# | tbl-cap: "2022-taxonomy classes by okrug (counts). Okrugs in rows, classes in columns."
cls = [x for x in c.CLASS_ORDER if (v3["category_2022"] == x).any()]
t = pd.crosstab(v3["okrug_key"], v3["category_2022"]).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER)
t = t.reindex(columns=cls, fill_value=0)
short = {"Grocery shops": "Grocery", "Alcohol shops": "Alcohol",
         "Tobacco outlets": "Tobacco", "Other (outside 2022 scheme)": "Other"}
Markdown(t.rename(columns=short).to_markdown())
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-recode-heat
# | fig-cap: "Within-okrug composition: each row sums to 100%. A single sequential hue encodes magnitude."
share = (t.div(t.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100).rename(columns=short)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
im = ax.imshow(share.values, cmap="Blues", aspect="auto", vmin=0)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(share.columns)), share.columns, rotation=35, ha="right", fontsize=8)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(share.index)), share.index, fontsize=8)
for i in range(share.shape[0]):
    for j in range(share.shape[1]):
        v = share.values[i, j]
        ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                color="white" if v > share.values.max() * 0.55 else INK)

ax.grid(False)
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="% of okrug")

plt.show()
```

## Health-supporting infrastructure vs. risk factors

Following the 2022 framing, `Medical` and `Sport` are health-supporting, and
`Alcohol shops`, `Tobacco outlets` and `Industrial` are risk factors.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-healthrisk
# | tbl-cap: "Health-supporting objects vs. risk factors by okrug, with the health-to-risk ratio. Counts are absolute; no population denominator is available in this delivery."
grp = np.where(v3["category_2022"].isin(c.HEALTH_CLASSES), "Health",
               np.where(v3["category_2022"].isin(c.RISK_CLASSES), "Risk", "Neutral"))
v3["grp"] = grp
t = pd.crosstab(v3["okrug_key"], v3["grp"]).reindex(OKRUG_ORDER)
t = t[["Health", "Risk", "Neutral"]]
t["Ratio H:R"] = (t["Health"] / t["Risk"]).round(2)
t.loc["CITY"] = [t["Health"].sum(), t["Risk"].sum(), t["Neutral"].sum(),
                 round(t["Health"].sum() / t["Risk"].sum(), 2)]
Markdown(t.to_markdown())
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-healthrisk
# | fig-cap: "Health-supporting infrastructure (blue) against risk factors (orange) per okrug."
tt = t.drop(index="CITY")
y = np.arange(len(tt))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.4))
ax.barh(y - 0.20, tt["Health"], height=0.38, color=ACCENT, label="Health-supporting (Medical, Sport)")
ax.barh(y + 0.20, tt["Risk"], height=0.38, color=RISK, label="Risk factors (Alcohol, Tobacco, Industrial)")
for i in range(len(tt)):
    ax.text(tt["Health"].iloc[i], i - 0.20, f" {tt['Health'].iloc[i]:,}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
    ax.text(tt["Risk"].iloc[i], i + 0.20, f" {tt['Risk'].iloc[i]:,}", va="center", fontsize=8, color=INK)
ax.set_yticks(y, tt.index, fontsize=8)
ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlabel("Objects")
ax.set_title("Health-supporting infrastructure vs. risk factors")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The city-wide ratio is 5.3 health-supporting objects per risk object. The spread
across okrugs (3.7 to 8.5) rests on small risk-side counts — the smallest okrugs
carry 2 to 6 risk objects each — so okrug-level ratios should be read as
indicative only. Risk objects are also the classes the export covers least well
(see @sec-provenance), which biases the ratio upward.

# Part IV — spatial distribution {#sec-map}

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of the 2026 export by okrug, on an OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemap."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.4))
for color, d in zip(sns.color_palette("colorblind", len(OKRUG_ORDER)), OKRUG_ORDER):
    sub = v3[v3["okrug_key"] == d]
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=5, alpha=0.55,
               color=color, label=f"{d} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("Objects by okrug — 2026 export")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.54)))
try:
    # Tiles are cached in data/tile_cache, so only the first render needs
    # internet access; offline we fall back to the plain scatter.
    import contextily as ctx
    tile_cache = c.ROOT / "data" / "tile_cache"
    tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
    ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                    attribution_size=5)
    ax.grid(visible=False)
except Exception:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=2.4, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Okrug colouring now follows visible spatial boundaries. The export spans
64.41–64.71 °N, covering the outlying northern and southern okrugs rather than
the centre alone.

The three okrugs covered by the 2022 study hold
`{python} f"{len(three):,}"` of the export's `{python} f"{n_obj:,}"` objects
(`{python} f"{len(three) / n_obj * 100:.0f}"` %). The record-level comparison
against the 2022 benchmark, including the confirmation map for those three
okrugs, is the subject of the companion report
(`reports/v3/eda-v3-validation.pdf`); its headline is that only **19 %** of the
2026 content in those okrugs has a 2022 counterpart, and that the contractor's
reported 94.3 % match rate does not survive independent re-checking.

# Part V — the commercial directory dump {#sec-base}

```{python}
# | label: load-base

n_base = len(base)
base_coords = base["latitude"].notna().sum()
base_district = base["Район города"].notna().sum()
```

`export_base_688669_zal6mp.xlsx` has no precedent in earlier deliveries:
`{python} f"{n_base:,}"` records across 25 fields, in a **third taxonomy**
(`Рубрика` / `Подрубрика` / `Тип подрубрики`) unrelated to either the export's
own categories or the 2022 scheme. It carries fields no other source has —
revenue analysis, online rating, review counts, messenger contacts.

```{python}
    ["Company type populated", f"{base['Тип компании'].notna().sum():,}", f"{base['Тип компании'].notna().mean() * 100:.0f}%"],
    ["Status 'active'", f"{(base['Статус'] == 'Действующая').sum():,}", "10 in liquidation"],
]

```

```{python}
# | label: fig-base-rubric
# | fig-cap: "Top 12 rubrics in the commercial dump. Its composition is business-directory-shaped, not infrastructure-shaped."
barh(base["Рубрика"].value_counts().head(12), "Commercial dump — top rubrics",
     "Records", color=PURPLE, figsize=(7.2, 4.8))
```

Two properties disqualify this file as a primary source. Its okrug field is
**empty for every record**, so okrug can only be recovered spatially; and its
coordinates are rounded to three decimals — roughly ±55 m at this latitude —
which is coarser than the 50 m radius used for record matching. It is usable as a
supplementary attribute source and as a weak third-party corroboration signal
(the companion report measures that corroboration at 3.6 % on name and address),
but it cannot replace or validate the main export.

# Part VI — the ARKTMED indicator panel {#sec-arktmed}

```{python}
# | label: load-ark
ark3 = c.load_arktmed()
ark2 = c.load_arktmed(c.V2_ARK)
ind3, ind2 = ark3["Показатели"], ark2["Показатели"]
ind3["section_en"] = ind3["Раздел"].map(c.SECTION_EN).fillna(ind3["Раздел"])


def linearity(ind):
    out = []
    for code, g in ind.groupby("Код показателя"):
        g = g.dropna(subset=["Значение"])
        if len(g) >= 3 and g["Значение"].std() > 0:
            out.append(np.corrcoef(g["Год"], g["Значение"])[0, 1] ** 2)
    return np.array(out)


lin3, lin2 = linearity(ind3), linearity(ind2)
```

::: {.callout-important}
## The synthetic-panel caveat no longer applies — but the panel lost its health indicators

The second delivery's panel was synthetic: **27 of its 27** testable series were
exactly linear in time (R² ≥ 0.999). In this delivery **0 of
`{python} f"{len(lin3)}"`** are, with a median R² of
`{python} f"{np.median(lin3):.2f}"`, and the sources are named Rosstat files
rather than portal home pages. The numbers are now citable. However, every
health-outcome indicator the previous panel carried — morbidity, mortality, life
expectancy, air pollution, emissions — has been **removed**, and the risk-index
sheet is empty.
:::

## Environmental indicators

```{python}
# | label: tbl-eco
# | tbl-cap: "The environment section in full. All four series are single-year 2025 expenditure figures."
eco = ind3[ind3["Раздел"] == "Экология"][["Показатель", "Год", "Значение", "Ед. изм."]]
eco = eco.rename(columns={"Показатель": "Indicator", "Год": "Year",
                          "Значение": "Value", "Ед. изм.": "Unit"})
eco["Value"] = eco["Value"].map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}")
Markdown(eco.to_markdown(index=False))
```

The environment section consists of four **2025-only expenditure lines**. They
describe municipal spending on environmental protection, not environmental
state — there is no air quality, emissions or water quality measure anywhere in
this delivery. The second delivery did carry `air_pollution_index`,
`emissions_total` and `water_quality_index`, but those series were synthetic and
are not recoverable.

```{python}
# | label: fig-climate
# | fig-cap: "The climate series — the only indicators covering the full 2021-2026 period. Values come from a reanalysis archive."
clim = ind3[ind3["Раздел"] == "Климат"]
show = ["Средняя температура", "Минимальная температура", "Максимальная температура"]

for ax, name, color in zip(axes, show, [ACCENT, GREEN, RISK]):
    s = clim[clim["Показатель"] == name].sort_values("Год")
    ax.plot(s["Год"], s["Значение"], marker="o", markersize=5, linewidth=2, color=color)
    ax.set_title(name[:26], fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("")
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
axes[0].set_ylabel("°C", fontsize=8)
fig.suptitle("Climate series, 2021–2026 (°C)", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Note that 2026 is incomplete at the time of this delivery: the panel's 2026
climate values cover a partial year and its economy series run to 2026 as well.
Treat the final year as provisional.

# Caveats {#sec-caveats}

- **Independent corroboration is rare.** 2.4 % of objects are confirmed by both
  providers; 89.6 % rest on OSM alone. The export's own
  `match_distance_meters` / `match_name_similarity` fields are a deduplication
  key, not independent verification.
- **`website_check_status` is empty for every record** and `opening_date_orig`
  is present for 0.6 %.
- **The `Grocery shops` class was empty in all previously delivered reports**
  (see @sec-recode). Any published count of `Other (outside 2022 scheme)` from
  the first- or second-delivery reports is inflated by roughly 800 objects.
- **`Industrial` is unreliable at this size.** It holds 25 objects, several of
  them name-substring false positives (a hostel, a jewellery shop). Do not read
  okrug-level industrial counts.
- **No population denominator** ships with this delivery, so all okrug
  comparisons are absolute counts. Okrug-level health-to-risk ratios rest on
  single-digit risk counts in the smaller okrugs.
- **The commercial dump cannot be used for okrug-level or record-level work** —
  empty okrug field, coordinates rounded to ±55 m.
- **The ARKTMED panel carries no health-outcome indicator** and its risk-index
  sheet is empty. Outside the climate series it is a two- to three-year snapshot,
  and its 2026 values are provisional.
- **Five okrugs remain unvalidated against any benchmark.** The 2022 study covers
  Lomonosovsky, Oktyabrsky and Maiskaya Gorka only; nothing in this delivery
  independently checks the other six.
